tagline: A 715 KB ternary decision model that plays four games at the oracle's level and answers typed questions in free text, above the majority class of the typed-decisions bench.
short_description: 715 KB model for four games and typed questions
notes: Published at full depth: its conformal early-exit thresholds were rejected by the pre-registered arena check.
0.480 on the typed-decisions bench, where the majority class is 0.398 and s5-lite reaches 0.696: expect mistakes on questions in free text.

tagline: A 250 KB ternary model that reads a pasted text and says whether it exposes a secret, which service issued it, what kind of value it is and on which line.
short_description: 250 KB model that spots exposed secrets in a text
notes: On a synthetic bench of file types it never saw, it beats a gitleaks-style rule scanner: secret 0.9990 against 0.977, service 0.9795 against 0.787. The bench comes from our own generator: it says nothing about real leaks in real repositories.
The line answer is weak (0.6859 on the bench): do not rely on it.
The preset keys are fake, generated in each provider's public format with a random body. Everything runs in your browser: nothing you paste is sent anywhere.

tagline: A 17M-parameter decision model whose options cannot see each other: reordering the options or renaming their keys cannot change an answer.
short_description: 17M decision model, invariant to option order and keys
notes: This checkpoint is a longer run (8,000 steps) added for the demo outside the pre-registered bets; see the results page for what failed and why.
It answers 21 of the 30 English demo cases: expect mistakes, especially on incidents and severity.

tagline: An experimental 5.6M ternary decision model with free-text options, distilled from Qwen3.5-4B in one night. It failed its quality gate.
notes: Published as a documented negative result: it scores below the majority class on the typed-decisions bench.
